summary.headline: Platinum Industries Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23.3% to INR 121.3 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.9% from 13.8% on freight and ramp-up costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 23.3% YoY to INR 121.3 crore, while EBITDA fell to INR 10.8 crore (8.9% margin) from INR 13.6 crore (13.8%) and PAT fell to INR 7.6 crore from INR 11 crore. H1 FY27 revenue rose 7.7% to INR 230.2 crore, with H1 PAT at INR 18.7 crore versus INR 24.1 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze to ocean freight costs, a lower share of high-margin lead-free PVC stabilisers, and the ramp-up of the expanded Palghar facility (utilisation about 30-35%). Egypt plant commissioning has slipped, with partial capacity now expected by 31 December 2026, and management reiterated 13-15% EBITDA margin for FY28.

segments.name: PVC stabilisers / CPVC additives (core)
segments.commentary: CPVC margin dipped about 1-2% QoQ; lead-free stabiliser margin fell 3-4% in the comparison cited. Lead-free share is temporarily lower, weighing on mix.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue about INR 24 crore in Q2 vs INR 22 crore in Q1, up about 40% YoY in Q2. Ocean freight rose to about INR 5 crore from about INR 2.5 crore on similar revenue.

segments.name: Platinum Oleo chemicals
segments.commentary: New segment; commenced sales of oleochemical derivatives and specialty chemicals, INR 11.4 crore in Q2 and INR 16.7 crore in H1 FY27, with India market development and export exploration underway.

segments.name: Rivadu Lifesciences
segments.commentary: Registered March 2026; signed exclusive sale and purchase agreement in September 2026 with South Korea's CAREGEN for Korglutide health functional food in India, with possible local manufacturing later. Pilot sale completed in first year; no revenue size disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Egypt plant: capacity raised from 30,000 MTPA (prospectus) to 60,000 MTPA; partial capacity by 31 December 2026, remainder by 31 March 2027. Management expects FY27 Egypt revenue of INR 25-30 crore, covering roughly Jan-mid March sales.
Management said Egypt contribution is meaningful from FY28 onward, with exports from India limited to East Africa, Bangladesh and neighbouring countries.
EBITDA margin: management reiterated 13-15% for FY28 and maintaining 13-15% year on year; said freight pressure should ease over the next two quarters, though no indication of easing yet.

Medium-term: about 35% revenue CAGR over three years cited; management declined to give a short-term FY27 revenue target. Earlier 35-40% FY27 growth view was implicitly reset; Egypt slippage cited as INR 30-35 crore of missed sales.
Palghar utilisation expected to cross about 50% within two years; rapid ramp expected over the next 1-1.5 years.
Rivadu/Korglutide: positioning strategy to be ready in 10-15 days; management said Q1 FY28 for pharma contribution.
capex_capacity: Palghar expanded facility utilisation about 30-35% (Q&A) and about 30% (later in call); target above 50% in about two years.

Egypt manufacturing facility: capacity raised to 60,000 MTPA; lead stabilisers to be commissioned first, other products to follow; capital advances to project suppliers by Egypt subsidiary drove other non-current assets up to INR 28.96 crore (Sept 2026) from INR 1.94 crore (March 2026).
Management said the company is debt-free to date; finance cost rise questioned by analyst was disputed by management.
demand_pricing: Industry: management cited a significant degrowth in PVC pipe industry demand for April-September 2026, with a major peer reporting 18-20% sales decline; pipe industry sales picked up from mid-September and grew in recent months.
Freight: ocean shipping costs are the main margin headwind; management does not expect them to fall in the next three to four months and sees no direct link between crude prices and polymer prices.
Domestic mix improved from October 2026 per management, after export-heavy Q1 and Q2.
Volume data for PVC and lead-free PVC was not shared; management offered offline follow-up.
Korglutide pricing: INR 10,000-12,000 per 30-day bottle, said to be 10-20% cheaper than Mounjaro and Ozempic.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the pipes industry in Q2 and whether falling crude prices will help.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a significant PVC pipe industry degrowth April-September, with a peer down 18-20%; said crude has no direct link to polymer prices and shipping costs are the real pressure, not expected to ease in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Why exports lifted revenue while margins fell, and whether freight is easing.
qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue was about INR 24 crore in Q2 (INR 22 crore in Q1); freight rose to INR 5 crore from INR 2.5 crore on similar revenue. No indication yet of freight easing, though management expects margins to recover over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for Egypt commissioning and any FY27 revenue from Egypt.
qa_highlights.answer: Expected FY27 Egypt revenue of INR 25-30 crore; stabiliser production to start by 31 December 2026 with sales over about 2.5 months (mid-January to March).

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin return to the 13-15% range in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management answered yes, absolutely, reiterating the 13-15% range.

qa_highlights.question: Palghar utilisation level and ramp plan.
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation around 30-35% (about 30% later in call); new customers added this year; target above 50% within two years.

qa_highlights.question: Causes of the revenue-to-profit gap: input costs vs competitive pricing, and why the 35-40% FY27 growth target was missed.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product margin declines were small (1-2% in CPVC QoQ; 3-4% in lead-free stabiliser). Missed Egypt sales of INR 30-35 crore due to later start; otherwise on track for about 35% three-year CAGR. Short-term guidance not given.

risks_watch: Ocean freight costs remain elevated; Q2 freight roughly doubled on similar export revenue and management has no visibility on relief.
Egypt commissioning is already behind earlier plan (partial start now by 31 December 2026); a slip would push FY27 Egypt revenue below INR 25-30 crore.
Palghar utilisation of about 30% keeps fixed costs and depreciation high; EBITDA margin fell to 8.9% in Q2 and 10.5% in H1.
Mix risk: lower share of high-margin lead-free stabilisers; management says lead-free margin fell 3-4%.
Management withheld volume data and short-term FY27 guidance, limiting visibility for the next quarter.
Rivadu/Korglutide is at an early stage; positioning and pricing still under study, with a pharma contribution expected from Q1 FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term structural growth and the 13-15% margin target, but cautious and at times vague on near-term numbers. Management did not give a revised FY27 revenue target, attributed the shortfall to freight costs and Egypt timing, and deflected volume and short-term guidance questions.

growth.why: Management declined to give an FY27 revenue target, withdrew the earlier 35-40% FY27 view (Egypt slipped, INR 30-35 cr missed sales) and cut FY27 Egypt revenue to INR 25-30 cr; growth now rests on a 35% three-year CAGR claim, Egypt capacity (partial by 31 Dec 2026) and Palghar ramp from 30-35% utilisation, with FY28 EBITDA margin of 13-15% held.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 8.9% from 13.8% and H1 is 10.5%, with management saying freight should ease over two quarters but showing no sign of it yet; reiterated 13-15% FY28 margin is a multi-quarter recovery path, not a near-term expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Egypt 60,000 MTPA plant is under construction with partial capacity by 31 Dec 2026 and remainder by 31 Mar 2027, though it has already slipped and FY27 Egypt revenue was cut to INR 25-30 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Export revenue rose to about INR 24 crore in Q2 from INR 22 crore in Q1 and Palghar utilisation is only 30-35%, but PVC pipe demand degrew in April-September with a peer down 18-20% and volume data was withheld.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is low at about 30% at Palghar, so there is no capacity pressure to justify new capex; the only pending spend is the Egypt project, with capital advances already at INR 28.96 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management withdrew its 35-40% FY27 growth view, gave no FY27 revenue target and cut Egypt FY27 revenue to INR 25-30 crore after INR 30-35 crore of missed sales.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight costs are not expected to ease for three to four months, Egypt commissioning has already slipped, and Q2 PAT fell to INR 7.6 crore from INR 11 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management guided pharma contribution from Rivadu/Korglutide in Q1 FY28 with pricing at INR 10,000-12,000 per bottle, though positioning is still at an early stage.

rows.label: Egypt plant ramp (lead stabilisers first)
rows.why: Partial capacity by 31 Dec 2026 with sales over about 2.5 months to March; Egypt contribution called meaningful from FY28, with exports limited to East Africa, Bangladesh and neighbours.

rows.label: Domestic mix recovery
rows.why: Management said domestic mix improved from October 2026 after export-heavy Q1 and Q2, but no volume data was shared to confirm it.

rows.label: Freight cost relief
rows.why: Ocean freight rose to about INR 5 crore from INR 2.5 crore on similar export revenue in Q2, and management does not expect shipping costs to fall in the next three to four months.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term 35% three-year CAGR and the 13-15% FY28 margin, but cautious and vague on near-term numbers, withholding volume data and FY27 revenue guidance; analysts pressed on the margin squeeze, freight costs, the missed FY27 growth target and finance costs.
